text: What are the more advanced RAG structures, with rerank, query expansion, etc.? There should be content about it, maybe more than one piece.
What are the categories of agent memory? I think one of them is episodic memory, and there are some others. Can you remind me what we read about this?
A piece by Facebook or Meta mentions an evaluation strategy with a weak and a strong model, with each model handling things differently. Can you remind me of the exact setup between the two?
On atomicity in evaluations, there was a piece proposing the idea. Besides atomicity, can you remind me of other important takeaways from it?
There was a piece saying a plain markdown file is better than a vector store. Can you remind me of its arguments?

Something about a markdown format, open knowledge format or something. It is a way to write a piece of knowledge to make it easier for an agent to look up. I need some help recovering it; can you search and remind me what it is about?

With voice agents, we read some content about safety in the voice output. The challenge is that voice interactions need lower latency, so it is not as simple as having a second LLM check the outputs. Can you remind me whether there are any other approaches or designs we read earlier?
Did we have a list of papers that should be read? I think it was meant for AI engineers or some role in the AI field.

There was a YouTube piece between a host and a guest. One takeaway I remember is that it talks about uncertainty with language models, maybe not uncertainty. The example they use is a self-driving car seeing road conditions unseen in its training data, and how it would handle the situation given the model's uncertainty.
I thought we read about some meditation approaches, like how to meditate. Can you find it and remind me what it says?
Did we cover any setups for running open-source language models on local devices, like what hardware, how, and cost?
One piece about how to sleep better: instead of the usual suggestions like meditation, it suggests something different.
A YouTube video by a monk, talking about life. It was inspiring, but I cannot recall it exactly.
I have read before about AI agents being agreeable and tending to agree with whatever the user says. Can you find the content providing the evidence and suggestions to deal with this?

Progressive disclosure, as I understand it at the moment, is about structuring context files so an agent can load documents only when needed; it is to deal with context window limitations. Can you remind me from past readings whether this is correct? Is there anything I am missing about the concept? Any critique of it?
Have we covered cooking with cast iron pans, or with stainless steel ones? What are the key things to be aware of?
On model fine-tuning, did we read anything about this topic and consider any applications of it, in personal or work projects?
Did we cover anything about being a good product manager? What is good vs bad?
Have we read anything about caring for indoor plants, like watering or soil choices?
Did we cover how to read papers, like the best approach to reading through a paper and still comprehending it well?

Did we read anything about approaches to fix a dropping attention span? The symptom is that my attention seems to have become short and I cannot focus for long. Was there any suggestion we read earlier?
Did we read about using lessons from Atomic Habits day to day to build a better life?
I need some advice on financial management, tips or suggestions for reacting to the AI bubble. Did we walk through anything in past readings?
Did we cover emotional resilience before? Something related to emotional intelligence, but not really the same.

With AI adoption at work, did we read anything about gradual implementation? It is really hard to shift straight from a conventional approach to AI-driven development. Was there any advice on adopting in phases or stages? Ideally relevant to the data stack, since I mostly do data work.
LLM wiki was popular sometime in 2026, and I want to build a personal version of it. Can you help me recall the content relevant to its implementation and design?
